story.opened: January 2026, in a former pub: soft launch 16 to 18 January, full launch 21 January.
story.then: The building is a roughly 175-year-old pub that was once The Globe and later a cafe. Chef Dara Klein first ran Tiella as a residency in the kitchen of the Compton Arms in Islington, then took this site in partnership with a childhood friend, Ry Jessup. Within weeks of opening, Time Out put it top of its list of the best new restaurants in London.
story.now: Open Wednesday to Sunday (as of February 2026). The menu is regional Italian: chicken Milanese, Venetian anchovies, and passatelli in broth were on it. The bar area is kept for walk-ins, with beer on tap including Guinness.
story.vibe: Still pubby after its refit: a handpainted sign, 1930s-style stained glass, mahogany panelling and, oddly, an enormous Cher portrait over the bar. Time Out called it a homely pub with 1960s vintage touches and candles.
worth_knowing: Dara Klein grew up working in her family's restaurant, Maria Pia's, in Wellington, New Zealand.
Time Out ranked Tiella number one in its list of London's best new restaurants in February 2026.
A giant portrait of Cher hangs above the bar.
